newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Oil Search says Kutubu qtr output falls.
newsitem.headline: Oil Search says Kutubu qtr output falls.

text.p: Papua New Guinea oil producer and explorer Oil Search Ltd said on Thursday that its share of crude oil output from the Kutubu oilfield in the nation's highlands region fell to 540,550 barrels in the calendar 1997 second quarter from 616,500 barrels in the first quarter.

Oil Search, which has a 7.763 percent stake in the field, said its share of daily output averaged 5,940 barrels per day in the latest quarter ended june 30. "Production was lower as a result of natural decline in the fields," the company said in its quarterly report. "Total Kutubu project cumulative production to the end of June 1997 was 199.2 million barrels."

The company said a development drilling campaign began in June with a series of wells planned to add production capacity to the Kutubu field. Oil production was expected to increase in the second half of 1997.

Chevron Corp's Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd unit is the field's operator and has a 19.375 percent holding. Other owners are The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd with 9.688 percent, BP Australia Ltd with 19.3785 percent, Mobil Oil Corp's Ampolex with 16.455 percent, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd with 4.844 percent, Orogen Minerals Ltd 15.75 percent and the Papua New Guinea government with 6.75 percent.

Oil Search said its second quarter revenue fell 11 percent to A$15.86 million from A$17.83 million in the March quarter, citing a 3.1 percent fall in liftings to 601,090 barrels and a fall in the average realised oil price to US$20.04 from US$22.07 in the March quarter.
